nodes.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le \exp\big((\log n)^{1/2 + \varepsilon}\big)$.
nodes.title: Chen's thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{3/8}$.
nodes.title: Fleury's thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, an element of $[0, \infty]$, is at least $4/5$.
nodes.title: Cube lower bound for the thin-shell variance constant

nodes.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C \log \log n$.
nodes.title: Guan's thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{1/3}$.
nodes.title: Guédon–Milman thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is isotropic log-concave when it is a probability measure, it has density $f$ with respect to Lebesgue measure for some log-concave density $f$, and for all coordinates $i, j$ the functions $x \mapsto x_i$ and $x \mapsto x_i x_j$ are $\mu$-integrable with $\int x_i \, d\mu(x) = 0$ and $\int x_i x_j \, d\mu(x) = \delta_{ij}$, that is, $1$ if $i = j$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Isotropic log-concave probability measures

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is a log-concave density when it is measurable, $f(x) \ge 0$ for every $x$, and $f(x)^{1-t} f(y)^t \le f((1-t)x + ty)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and every real $t$ with $0 < t < 1$.
nodes.title: Log-concave densities

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha = \big(1 + 7\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{53 - 4\sqrt{2}}\big)/8$. There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C (\log n)^{\alpha}$.
nodes.title: Jambulapati–Lee–Vempala thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C (\log n)^4$.
nodes.title: Klartag–Lehec polylogarithmic thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: There is a real $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n \ge 1$ and every isotropic log-concave measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ is at most $C$.
nodes.title: Klartag–Lehec thin-shell variance bound

nodes.summary: There is a real $C > 0$ such that for every natural number $n \ge 1$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C$.
nodes.title: Klartag–Lehec bounded thin-shell width

nodes.summary: There are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 3$ such that for every natural number $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ of dimension $n$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C \sqrt{n / \log n}$.
nodes.title: Klartag's first thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a constant $C > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 3$ such that for every dimension $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{2/5 + \varepsilon}$. Here $\sigma_n$ is the square root of the supremum of $\mathbb{E}\,(|X| - \sqrt{n})^2$ over isotropic log-concave random vectors $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: Klartag's power-law thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: There are a constant $C > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 3$ such that for every dimension $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C \sqrt{\log n}$. Here $\sigma_n$ is the square root of the supremum of $\mathbb{E}\,(|X| - \sqrt{n})^2$ over isotropic log-concave random vectors $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Klartag's square-root-logarithmic thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: There are a constant $C > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 3$ such that for every dimension $n \ge N$ the thin-shell width $\sigma_n \in [0, \infty]$ satisfies $\sigma_n \le C n^{1/4}$. Here $\sigma_n$ is the square root of the supremum of $\mathbb{E}\,(|X| - \sqrt{n})^2$ over isotropic log-concave random vectors $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: Lee–Vempala thin-shell bound

nodes.summary: The thin-shell variance constant bounds the normalized radius variance of isotropic log-concave measures. For every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is at most the thin-shell variance constant.
nodes.title: The thin-shell variance constant bounds the normalized radius variance of isotropic log-concave measures

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is $\frac{1}{n} \int (\|x\|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$, where $\|x\|$ is the Euclidean norm (for $n = 0$ the integral is $0$ and so is the value).
nodes.title: Normalized radius variance

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $r \ge 0$ and $d > 0$, $(r - \sqrt{d})^2 \le (r^2 - d)^2 / d$.
nodes.title: Elementary radius deviation bound

nodes.summary: For every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the integral $\int (\|x\| - \sqrt{n})^2 \, d\mu(x)$, taken in $[0, \infty]$ with $\|x\|$ the Euclidean norm, is at most the thin-shell variance constant.
nodes.title: The thin-shell variance constant bounds the radius fluctuation

nodes.summary: For every $n > 0$ and every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the integral $\int (\|x\| - \sqrt{n})^2 \, d\mu(x)$, taken in $[0, \infty]$ with $\|x\|$ the Euclidean norm, is at most the normalized radius variance of $\mu$.
nodes.title: Radius fluctuation is bounded by the normalized radius variance

nodes.summary: For every dimension $n \ge 1$, the standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is isotropic log-concave (a probability measure with a log-concave Lebesgue density, mean $0$ and identity covariance), and its normalized radius variance $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\gamma_n(x)$ equals $2$.
nodes.title: The standard Gaussian has normalized radius variance 2

nodes.summary: For every $C \in [0, \infty]$, the thin-shell variance constant is at most $C$ if and only if, for every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is at most $C$.
nodes.title: Characterization of bounds on the thin-shell variance constant

nodes.summary: If $C$ is a real number such that for every $n > 0$ and every isotropic log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ the normalized radius variance of $\mu$ is at most $\max(C, 0)$, then the thin-shell variance constant is finite.
nodes.title: A uniform variance bound makes the thin-shell variance constant finite

nodes.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the normalized radius variances $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all dimensions $n \ge 1$ and all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, is finite.
nodes.title: The thin-shell variance constant is finite

nodes.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, a value in $[0, \infty]$, is at least $0$.
nodes.title: The thin-shell variance constant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Write $|x|$ for the Euclidean norm. The thin-shell variance constant is the supremum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the normalized radius variance $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all dimensions $n \ge 1$ and all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: Thin-shell variance constant

nodes.summary: For every dimension $n \ge 1$, the thin-shell width in dimension $n$ is at most the square root of the thin-shell variance constant, computed in $[0, \infty]$ with $\sqrt{\infty} = \infty$.
nodes.title: Thin-shell width is at most the square root of the variance constant

nodes.summary: Write $|x|$ for the Euclidean norm. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the thin-shell width in dimension $n$ is the square root of the supremum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of $\int (|x| - \sqrt{n})^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $\sqrt{\infty} = \infty$.
nodes.title: Thin-shell width

nodes.summary: The thin-shell variance constant, the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the normalized radius variances $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ over all dimensions $n \ge 1$ and all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, is at least $2$.
nodes.title: The thin-shell variance constant is at least 2

nodes.summary: For every dimension $n \ge 1$, let $\mu$ be the uniform probability measure on the cube $[-\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3}]^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (Lebesgue measure restricted to the cube and divided by its volume). Then $\mu$ is isotropic log-concave (a probability measure with a log-concave Lebesgue density, mean $0$ and identity covariance), and its normalized radius variance $\frac{1}{n} \int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x)$…
nodes.title: The isotropic cube has normalized radius variance 4/5

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
